content.text:
Your analytics are empty because this repository currently has:

- Entire enabled
- zero Entire checkpoints
- zero captured sessions
- only the Claude Code integration installed
- no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers in existing commits

Ordinary Git commits and `Co-Authored-By` lines do not generate Entire analytics. Entire.io reads captured checkpoints from the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. [Entire documentation](https://docs.entire.io/quickstart)

To capture this Codex session:

```powershell
entire agent add codex
```

Then completely restart Codex from the repository root. The integration must be installed before the session starts.

After Codex makes a tracked file change:

```powershell
entire status
git add <files>
git commit -m "Your commit"
entire checkpoint list
git push
```

Accept the prompt to link the commit to the active session. Afterward, `entire checkpoint list` should show at least one checkpoint, and `git push` will synchronize the checkpoint branch used by Entire.io. [Codex integration guide](https://docs.entire.io/agents/codex)

For Claude, its hooks are already present in [.claude/settings.json](C:/Users/marks/Documents/entire-viktor-tumai-ehk/.claude/settings.json:2), but Claude must also be restarted after installation.

Historical Claude work may be recoverable with:

```powershell
entire import claude-code --dry-run
entire import claude-code
git push
```

However, the current repository inspection found no imported checkpoints. Old work cannot be reconstructed merely from commit messages.

Important: checkpoint history includes transcripts. Because this challenge dataset must not be redistributed, inspect the checkpoint data and ensure no raw trajectory content was captured before pushing—especially to a public repository. [Entire security documentation](https://docs.entire.io/security)
